chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

Al-Hakam ibn 'Utainah said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man to whom a domestic pigeon was gifted while he was in the sanctuary (Haram) but not from the sanctuary, and he said: 'If it is even (balanced), you let it go free; and if it is not so, you do well by it (keep it) until its feathers become even, then you let it go free.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who receives a bird as a gift while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the distinction between 'killing' (which incurs a penalty) and 'releasing' (which does not) for a muhrim who receives a gift of a bird. The ruling hinges on the bird's physical state: if it is already 'even' (stable/ready to fly), it is released immediately; if not, the pilgrim nurtures it until it reaches that state, ensuring the act is one of liberation rather than slaughter. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the intent and physical condition of the animal in determining the applicability of the fidya (expiation).
